pronunciation.body:
The ​reconstructed ‌pronunciation of ‌the ​name ​is ​**/ˈjoʊni/** — ​Sanskrit ​(IAST: ‌Yoni).[^1]

​Phoneme by ​phoneme:

- ‌**Yo-** ​— ‌The root ​is ‌√yu, ​“to ​unite, join” ​— ​the ​same ‌yu-family as ​yoga’s ‌yoking.
- ​**-ni** ‌— The ​feminine ‌noun: ​“womb”, ‌“source”, “place ​of ​origin”.
- ‌**** ‌— The ‌feminine ​principle, ​the ‌origin — ​paired ​with ‌the ​liṅga in ​Śaiva ‌worship.

​For ‌the modern ​speaker, ​the ​closest ​approximation is: ‌“YOH-nee”

‌Kindred ​and ‌historical forms ​of ​the ‌name:

- ‌**Counterpart** — ‌liṅga ‌— ​the ‌mark; together ​the ​Śaiva ​aniconic ‌pair
- **Root** ​— ​√yu ​— ‌to unite; ​the ​same ​family ‌as yoga

​The ‌word ​means ‌womb, source, ​and ‌place ‌of ​origin — ​the ​feminine ​as ‌the container ‌of ​creation.

domains.body:
**Yoni** ​is the ‌source: ‌the womb, ​the origin-place, ​the ​feminine principle ​that ​the Śaiva ‌tradition pairs ​with ​the liṅga ‌as ​the two-in-one ‌of ​all generation. ‌In philosophy ​it ​names the ​material ​cause — ​prakṛti, ‌the matrix ​from which ‌the ​differentiated world ‌flows; ​in ritual ‌it is ​the ‌altar’s base, ​the ​goddess’s body, ‌and ‌the cosmic ‌ground on ​which ​the god ‌stands.[^1]

### ​The Liṅga-Yoni

​The ‌Śaiva aniconic ​pair: the ​standing ‌mark in ​the ‌flowing base ​— creation ​and ​its ground, ​united.

### ‌The Material ‌Cause

​In Sāṃkhya-Yoga, ‌prakṛti the ​yoni ​is the ‌womb ‌of the ‌world ‌— all ​effects pre-exist ‌in ​their cause.

### ​The ​Goddess’s Body

‌In the ​Śākta ​traditions the ​yoni ‌is the ​goddess ​herself — ​the pīṭha, ‌the ​sacred seat ‌of ​power.

### The ‌Ritual ​Base

Every ‌Śaiva altar’s ‌foundation ​is the ​yoni-shaped ​basin, catching ​the libation ‌that ‌feeds the ​god.

symbols.body:
The ​iconography ‌associated ‌with Yoni ​concentrates ​in ​a ​small ​set ‌of recurring ​attributes, ​each ‌a ​compressed ‌statement ​about ‌the name:[^1]

- ​**The ​Liṅga-Yoni** ​— ​The ​Śaiva ‌aniconic pair: ​the ‌standing ​mark ‌in ​the ‌flowing base ​— ‌creation ​and ​its ‌ground, ‌united.
- ‌**The Material ​Cause** ​— ‌In ​Sāṃkhya-Yoga, ​prakṛti ‌the yoni ​is ​the ‌womb ​of ‌the ​world — ​all ​effects ​pre-exist ‌in ‌their ​cause.
- **The ‌Goddess’s ​Body** ​— ‌In ‌the ‌Śākta ‌traditions the ​yoni ‌is ​the ​goddess ​herself ‌— the ​pīṭha, ​the ​sacred ‌seat ​of ​power.
- **The ​Ritual ‌Base** ​— ‌Every ​Śaiva ‌altar’s ​foundation is ‌the ‌yoni-shaped ​basin, ​catching ​the ​libation that ‌feeds ‌the ​god.

mythology.body:
The yoni’s ​mythology is the ‌Śaiva theology of the ‌pair: the god ​and his power, ​the liṅga and its ​base, the still ​and the flowing. ​Its narratives are the ‌Goddess-traditions’ own — ​Satī’s sacrifice, the ​dismembered pīṭhas, and ‌the tantric ritual in ​which the base ‌is the goddess’s ​body receiving the god’s ‌libation. The word ​itself is the ​doctrine: the womb ​as the world’s first ​fact.[^1]

### The Endless ​Pillar and Its ‌Base (Liṅga Purāṇa)

The ​tradition’s founding image: ‌the endless pillar ​of fire — the ‌liṅga without top ​or bottom — ‌that humbled Brahmā ​and Vishnu, standing in ‌the yoni-base as ​the ground of ​the ground. The Purāṇa’s ‌theology is exact: ‌the mark is ‌the god, the ​base is his power, ​and worship of ‌the one without ​the other is incomplete.[^2]

### ​The Dismembered Seat ‌(Satī Cycle)

When ​Satī self-immolated at her ​father’s insult, Śiva ‌wandered the world ​with her corpse, ‌and the pieces fell ​as the śakti-pīṭhas ​— each a ​seat of the goddess’s ​power, each in ‌some tellings marked ‌by the yoni. The ​tantric pilgrimages map ‌the goddess’s body ​onto the subcontinent: ​the womb as sacred ‌geography.

### The Rite ‌of the Base ‌(Tantric Ritual)

In the ‌tantric pūjā the ​yoni-basin receives the ‌libations poured over ​the liṅga, channelling the ​offering to the ​goddess below. The ‌ritual grammar is the ​theology in action: ​creation as the ​union of the standing ‌god and the ​flowing ground, generation ​as worship.

### The ​Matrix of Causes (Sāṃkhya ‌Philosophy)

The Sāṃkhya ​makes yoni technical: ‌prakṛti, the material cause, ​is the womb ‌in which all ​effects pre-exist — ‌the tree in the ‌seed, the world ​in the matrix. ​The doctrine of satkāryavāda, ​‘the effect pre-exists ​in the cause’, ‌is the philosophy of ‌the yoni stated ​as metaphysics.

overview.body:
**Yoni** ​(*yoni*) — ‌The Womb, ‌the Feminine ​Principle · ​'Womb, source' ​— the ​feminine principle, ​the origin ‌from which ​all creation ​flows — ‌belongs to ​the Sanskrit ‌tradition, where ​it ‌is catalogued ​under the ​domain "Source, ​Womb, Shakti". ​The name ​means "'Womb, ‌source' — ​the feminine ‌principle, the ​origin from ‌which all ​creation flows"[^1].

‌**Yoni** is ​the ‌source: the ​womb, the ​origin-place, the ‌feminine principle ‌that the ‌Śaiva tradition ​pairs with ​the liṅga ‌as the ​two-in-one of ​all generation. ‌In philosophy ​it names ​the material ‌cause ​— prakṛti, ‌the matrix ​from which ​the differentiated ​world flows; ​in ritual ‌it is ‌the altar’s ​base, the ‌goddess’s body, ​and the ​cosmic ground ‌on which ‌the god ‌stands.[^2]

the-name.body:
